title: Scaling and Rolling Updates
intro: Deployments make scaling and updating painless. Let's scale 'web' up, then push an image update, then roll it back.

steps.explanation: This just updates the desired replica count — the ReplicaSet controller handles creating the extra pods.
steps.why: You could also change the replica count with 'kubectl edit deployment web' or a 'kubectl patch', but 'scale' is the direct, scriptable way to do exactly this one thing without risking an accidental edit elsewhere.

steps.prompt: Update the nginx container image to nginx:1.25.
steps.explanation: By default this triggers a RollingUpdate — old pods are replaced gradually so there's no downtime.
steps.why: You could 'kubectl edit deployment web' and change the image by hand, but 'set image' targets exactly one field — no risk of fat-fingering something else in the spec while you're in there.

steps.fake_output:
Waiting for deployment "web" rollout to finish: 3 out of 5 new replicas have been updated...
deployment "web" successfully rolled out
steps.explanation: This blocks until the rollout finishes or fails — handy in scripts/CI.
steps.why: You could poll 'kubectl get pods' repeatedly to eyeball progress, but 'rollout status' is purpose-built for this — it blocks and reports done/failed automatically, which is what you actually want in a deploy script.

steps.prompt: Uh oh, turns out nginx:1.25 has a bug. Roll back to the previous version.
steps.explanation: Kubernetes keeps a revision history so you can undo instantly without remembering the old image tag.
steps.why: The alternative is re-running 'set image' with the old tag — 'rollout undo' is better because you don't have to remember or look up what that old tag even was.

steps.prompt: Check the rollout history to confirm.
steps.explanation: Tip: use --record or a change-cause annotation in real usage so this history is actually readable later.
steps.why: This is the only real way to see past revisions — 'kubectl get deployment -o yaml' only shows the current spec, not what changed or when.
